newsitem.title: UK: Spain's Ecu bond could surface next week - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Ecu bond could surface next week - bankers.

text.p: Spain could launch a long-awaited Ecu eurobond next week, bankers said on Friday.
In April, Spain announced it was planning a 2.0 billion Ecu ($2.2 billion) bond. It said the issue would have a 10-year maturity.
So far, the deal has not materialised, but bankers said Spain could come to the market soon.
"We are most likely expecting Spain's Ecu bond next week," a trader at a European bank said.
"The issue is expected to be smaller than the 2.0 billion Ecu originally planned, though, maybe at around 1.0 billion Ecu," he said.

Other bankers said the maturity would be slightly more than 10 years to match that of existing Bonos. The bonds could then be fungible after European economic and monetary union (EMU), planned for 1999.
Bankers said there was no mandate for the bond yet.
-- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748 ($ = 0.893 European Currency Unit ECUs)
